solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Livery of ambassador having soft touch while in charge

blocks.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a pat is a soft touch
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge; while just adds it on

explanation.surface: A diplomat's uniform, worn by someone gentle but in command.
explanation.walkthrough: "Livery" looks like a uniform, but here it is the adjective from liver, as in a livery complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatic means relating to the liver, which is what livery can mean.

clue.text: Cloth vanishes mysteriously, first bit of velvet left

indicators.note: things that happen mysteriously happen in no predictable order, so the letters are scrambled
only the opening letter of velvet is wanted
the velvet's first letter has left, so it is taken out of the fodder

blocks.note: used as printed
the first letter of velvet, removed

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric disappears strangely, leaving only a scrap of velvet behind.
explanation.walkthrough: VANISHES loses its V to leave ANISHES, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse cloth woven from jute or hemp.

clue.text: Links what is to be expected there

definitions.text: Links what is to be expected there

blocks.note: reads as connections or ties; the setter means a golf links, a seaside golf course

blocks.clueFragment: what is to be expected there
blocks.note: reads as a general forecast; on a golf course, the expected score for each hole has its own name

explanation.walkthrough: A links is a golf course, and par is the score expected there; the phrase also means anything normal or predictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Par for the course is literally the expected score on a golf links, and figuratively what one would expect.

clue.text: Party-pooper’s bloomer!

blocks.note: the letters sit across the hyphen, the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A killjoy has made an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the hyphen, so the eye reads past it. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a printing or typing blunder, and a bloomer is a blunder.

clue.text: Game, North American game in court

indicators.note: the American game sits in the court abbreviation

blocks.note: roque is a mallet-and-hoop game played on hard courts in the USA
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A list of sports, one of them North American and played indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Roque takes its name from croquet with the outer letters dropped, so the answer contains its own offshoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game played with mallets, balls and hoops.

clue.text: Cut crosswise badly, we won’t be involved

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, out of their proper order
W and E are told to stay out of the mix

blocks.note: used as printed
used as printed, and removed

explanation.surface: Someone has cut something across clumsily and we want no part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: CROSSWISE minus W and E leaves CROSSIS, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb from the tool: to scissor something is to cut it with scissors.

clue.text: Last character in assortment of riches made lively movements

indicators.note: the last character goes in the jumbled letters
an assortment mixes things up, so the letters of riches are rearranged

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
used as printed

explanation.surface: The last item in a pile of wealth made some sprightly moves.
explanation.walkthrough: "Last character" is not the last letter of a nearby word but of the whole alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzi, plural of scherzo, are lively movements in symphonies and sonatas.

clue.text: Resistance three times leaving belligerent warrior state

indicators.note: the three Rs leave the warrior
a belligerent warrior is in a disordered, fighting state, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance, taken three times
used as printed

explanation.surface: Opposition keeps deserting an aggressive soldier's cause.
explanation.walkthrough: WARRIOR has exactly three Rs; removing them leaves WAIO, which is rearranged. "State" looks like a condition but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iowa is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Refuse to change one’s resolve not to disarm

blocks.note: the idiom for holding firm
read literally, keeping hold of one's weapons

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the idiom literally: someone who sticks to their guns keeps hold of their weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to one's guns is to refuse to back down, and literally never to put down one's weapons.

clue.text: Artillerymen follow scramble to get on

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to trace is to follow

explanation.surface: Gunners fall in behind a rush to board.
explanation.walkthrough: "Get on" means get ahead in life, not climb aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the competitive scramble to get on in one's career.

clue.text: Expose oneself? Not half!

blocks.note: reads as indecent exposure; the setter means taking clothes off
reads as the British slang for 'definitely!'; the setter means literally only half the body is bared

explanation.walkthrough: "Not half!" is British slang for an emphatic yes, but read literally it says the exposure stops at half the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip to the waist is to bare the upper half of the body only.

clue.text: Prince or king cobra appearing alternately

indicators.note: only every other letter of king cobra shows up

blocks.note: the even letters: kInG cObRa

explanation.surface: A choice between royalty and a dangerous snake, turning up in turns.
explanation.walkthrough: "King" looks like a second royal definition, but it is part of the snake's name and part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the hero of Borodin's opera.

clue.text: Rush charioteer really heartlessly

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the outer letters of really remain

blocks.note: Judah Ben-Hur, the charioteer of the novel and film, is of the house of Hur
the first and last letters of really

explanation.surface: A chariot driver races along with genuine cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous charioteer is Ben-Hur; Ben means son of, so the family name is Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rush and to hurry both mean to move or act with haste.

clue.text: One bird going forwards or a number going back

indicators.note: the several birds are read backwards

blocks.note: a number of birds: auks, several of them

explanation.surface: A single bird flying ahead, or a flock heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are birds: one skua read forwards, several auks read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the skua, a gull-like seabird that robs others of their catch, is one bird among many.

clue.text: Not being so well, grain processor did not start

indicators.note: the miller loses the first letter

blocks.note: a miller grinds grain

explanation.surface: A miller felt unwell and so the mill never got going.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the M from MILLER leaves ILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Iller, a comparative of ill, describes someone not being so well.

clue.text: Second one’s during afternoon having sudden convulsive action

indicators.note: one's comes during the afternoon, so it sits inside PM

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
PM is the afternoon
one is A, and the 's is added as S

explanation.surface: Someone's second attempt at something one afternoon brought on a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of "one's" is kept as a letter, turning A into AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary gloss: the medical sense is an involuntary muscle contraction, which comes on suddenly and convulsively.

clue.text: Isn’t allowed to include electronic sheet

indicators.note: the phrase takes the electronic letter inside it

blocks.note: is not allowed is not let
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A rule that no electronic paper may be included.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sheet" looks like a sheet of anything, but here it is a small sheet of notepaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet of notepaper.

clue.text: Upgrade one member with dog with no tail

indicators.note: the dog loses its last letter

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Someone is upgraded by joining a club and getting a tailless dog.
explanation.walkthrough: ROVER loses its final R to become ROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean making something better than it was.

clue.text: Not the real reason expert suffered taking time

indicators.note: the expert has suffered a knock and comes out in a different shape

blocks.note: used as printed
T is the abbreviation for time, taken into the fodder

explanation.surface: An excuse that a specialist was hurt and took time off.
explanation.walkthrough: The T joins EXPERT before the rearranging, so the fodder is EXPERT plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one.

clue.text: Undeserved criticism having trophies recently stolen

blocks.note: pots is slang for trophies, silver cups
hot goods are recently stolen

explanation.surface: Unfair blame falls on someone after the club's cups go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls differently in the answer: POTS HOT becomes POT-SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative: a shot taken casually at an easy target becomes a cheap, unfair jibe.

clue.text: Weather report

blocks.note: a stormy kind of weather, heard rather than seen
a report is a loud bang, as of a gun

explanation.walkthrough: "Weather report" reads as a forecast, but report here is a loud bang, like the report of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is a kind of weather and also a loud report.

clue.text: Going round New Jersey first support dog

indicators.note: support and first go round New Jersey

blocks.note: a base supports what stands on it
NJ is the postal abbreviation of New Jersey
I is the Roman numeral one, as in first

explanation.surface: Travelling around New Jersey, first back a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: "First" is the Roman numeral for one, the first number; it joins the support on the outside of the state.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a small barkless hunting dog from central Africa.

clue.text: Mammal twice changing sex becoming fish

indicators.note: female F becomes male M, and it happens to both Fs

blocks.note: the buffalo is a mammal
each F, female, is swapped for M, male

explanation.surface: An animal switches sex twice and ends up a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: F and M are the standard abbreviations for female and male, so BUFFALO turns into BUMMALO.
explanation.definitionFit: The bummalo is a small South Asian fish, dried and sold as Bombay duck.

clue.text: Single new position as alternative

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
stead is a place or position, as in in someone's stead

explanation.surface: A lone person takes up a fresh post as a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Stead survives mainly in phrases like in his stead, meaning in his place.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases mean in place of the thing first expected.

clue.text: Attempt to circumvent initial oil film

indicators.note: the attempt goes around the letter
only the first letter of oil is used

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
the first letter of oil

explanation.surface: An effort to dodge an oily layer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Film" looks like the oily layer on the surface, but it is a cinema film.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 2004 Brad Pitt epic of the Trojan War bears the city's name.

clue.text: Couple’s short time in cathedral

blocks.note: a duo is a couple
mo is short for moment

explanation.surface: A pair has only a brief spell inside a great church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is "has": the couple has a short time. Mo, as in half a mo, is British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: the Italian name for a city's cathedral, as in Florence's Duomo.

clue.text: Goddess was present more than once

indicators.note: the same piece is used twice in a row

blocks.note: change was to the present tense of the same verb
the same IS again

explanation.surface: A goddess attended more than one occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: "Was present" means attended, but read as grammar it asks for the present tense of was.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood.

clue.text: No end of spicy food for one from Riga perhaps

indicators.note: the dish loses its final letter

blocks.note: a balti is a spicy curry, a British curry-house staple

explanation.surface: A Latvian gets no end of curry.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTI loses its I; "perhaps" marks Riga as just one example of a Baltic city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balt is a native of a Baltic state, such as Latvia, whose capital is Riga.

clue.text: She arranged to leave tumbledown teashop at the peak

indicators.note: the letters of she leave the teashop
a tumbledown building has fallen out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of she, in any order
used as printed

explanation.surface: A woman arranged to quit a ramshackle tea room on the mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: S, H and E are scattered through TEASHOP, hence "arranged"; removing them leaves TAOP to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a one-word preposition for on the very top of something.

clue.text: Heartland fraud’s breaking rigid regulation

indicators.note: the words are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: used as printed, the S of the possessive included

explanation.surface: A swindle in the country's interior is flouting strict rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: hard and fast means fixed and unbending, so the phrase is a rule that allows no exceptions.

clue.text: Speaker, one making birdlike noises?

blocks.note: a loudspeaker, specifically the small one in a hi-fi that handles high notes
one who tweets

explanation.walkthrough: A tweeter is the small loudspeaker for high notes; the question mark covers the made-up sense of someone who tweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a treble loudspeaker, and literally one who tweets like a bird.

clue.text: Not in favour of a little work, having been a model

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
a model poses

explanation.surface: Someone resents a small job after their modelling days.
explanation.walkthrough: "A little work" is a shortened word for work, not a small task.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be opposed to something is to be against it.
